- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 2–5%.
- If sentiment is negative or neutral (≤0.20), model frequently underestimates; increase forecast by 3–7% to compensate.
- Model shows persistent lag in mean reversion: if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast tends to stay above; adjust downward by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts early in the forecast window (days 1–7); cap first 5 days’ forecast at 1% below true 30-day average.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
